title: Situer une durée et une fête
summary: Choose present or compound past with negative depuis and use natural holiday date expressions.
objectives: Distinguish an ongoing negative state from the absence of a completed event.
Contrast depuis, pendant, il y a and en.
Use à with common festivals and feminine saint's-day names.

sources.label: B1 public topic index (coverage reference only)

sections.title: An ongoing absence is not always the same kind of absence
paragraphs: Depuis marks a starting point or elapsed duration reaching the reference time. For a state or habit that is still true now, use the present, even where English uses have been: Je ne travaille plus ici depuis juin, I have not worked here since June / I no longer work here and have not since June.

To say that a particular type of completed event has not occurred during the interval, the negative passé composé is often appropriate: Je n'ai pas reçu de réponse depuis lundi, I have not received a reply since Monday. Compare Je ne reçois plus de courrier depuis lundi, which presents an ongoing stopped delivery pattern. Do not use a mechanical rule that all negative depuis sentences take the same tense.

Present and compound past can overlap when a verb can describe either a state or repeated events. The exercises specify the intended viewpoint and sometimes the tense explicitly; they do not reject another natural viewpoint in an unconstrained conversation.
points: Vocabulary: une réponse (feminine), a reply; le courrier (masculine), mail.
The choice depends on aspect, the way the situation is viewed, as well as time.

examples.french: Je **ne fume plus depuis** trois ans.
examples.english: I haven't smoked for three years.
examples.note: A continuing non-smoking habit is described in the present.

examples.english: She hasn't lived here since January.

examples.french: Nous **n'avons reçu aucune réponse depuis** mardi.
examples.english: We haven't received any reply since Tuesday.
examples.note: No completed receipt event has occurred in the interval.

examples.french: Il **n'a pas appelé depuis** notre réunion.
examples.english: He hasn't called since our meeting.
examples.note: No call has occurred since the starting point.

mistakes.avoid: J'habite ici depuis il y a trois ans.
mistakes.why: For the ordinary elapsed-duration expression, use depuis directly with the duration. Il y a is not needed.

sections.title: Four different time questions
paragraphs: Depuis answers since when or for how long up to the reference time. Pendant marks the duration of an activity without saying it continues now. Il y a + duration places a past event that long ago. En + duration gives the time needed to complete something. These expressions are not interchangeable translations of English for.
Pour + duration can describe an intended span, particularly a planned stay or commitment: je pars pour trois jours. The context determines whether a duration is completed, ongoing or planned.
points: Use the tense and time expression together; a duration word alone does not settle every tense choice.

examples.english: I worked there for six months.

examples.french: Elle a terminé le dossier **en** deux heures, **il y a** trois jours.
examples.english: She finished the file in two hours, three days ago.
examples.note: Completion time differs from distance back in time.

sections.title: Choose the whole holiday expression
paragraphs: Common time expressions include à Noël, at Christmas, and à Pâques, at Easter, normally without an article in these standard expressions. Use à la Toussaint, at All Saints' Day, and au Nouvel An, at New Year. Le jour de Noël names the day itself. Pour Noël can instead express a plan, gift occasion or target date, depending on context; it is not always a wrong substitute.

Some regional or traditional usage says à la Noël. The exercises asking for the common no-article expression explicitly specify that choice. Dates such as le 14 juillet use a date article rather than an automatic à. Learn the phrase, not a universal rule that every celebration follows one article pattern.
points: Vocabulary: la Toussaint (feminine), All Saints' Day; le Nouvel An (masculine), New Year; Noël is normally treated as masculine in modern general use, with feminine regional/traditional usage also found.
A cultural date expression does not imply that everyone celebrates that occasion.

examples.french: Le centre sera fermé **à Noël**, mais ouvert **à Pâques**.
examples.english: The centre will be closed at Christmas but open at Easter.
We will meet again at New Year.

sections.title: The implied fête explains la
paragraphs: A celebration named for a saint commonly takes la because the implied noun is la fête, a celebration: à la Saint-Valentin, à la Saint-Patrick, à la Saint-Jean, à la Sainte-Catherine. The saint's gender controls Saint/Sainte in the name, but not the feminine article of the feast.
Distinguish the saint from the festival: saint Patrick refers to the person; la Saint-Patrick refers to the day. Festival names use a capital and a hyphen in these expressions.
points: Vocabulary: une fête (feminine), a celebration; la Saint-Valentin (feminine), Valentine's Day.

examples.french: L'association organise un repas **à la Saint-Patrick**.
examples.english: The association organizes a meal on Saint Patrick's Day.
examples.note: La refers to the celebration, not to the male saint.

examples.french: Un atelier sera proposé **à la Sainte-Catherine**.
examples.english: A workshop will be offered on Saint Catherine's Day.
examples.note: Sainte agrees with the saint's name, while the festival remains feminine.

mistakes.avoid: Nous organisons un concert au Saint-Patrick.
mistakes.prefer: Nous organisons un concert à la Saint-Patrick.
mistakes.why: The celebration takes la, with an implied feminine fête, not le for the saint.

practice.prompt: Use the present of travailler for an ongoing situation: Je ne ___ plus la nuit depuis mai.
practice.explanation: The present describes the continuing changed work pattern.

practice.prompt: Use the passé composé of recevoir: Je n'___ aucune lettre depuis jeudi.
practice.explanation: No receipt event has occurred during the interval.

practice.prompt: Use à, with an article only if required in the usual modern expression: ___ Noël. Do not use the regional à la Noël variant.
practice.explanation: The usual modern expression is à Noël, without an article.

practice.prompt: Supply the preposition and article: ___ Saint-Valentin.
practice.explanation: The feast uses an implied feminine fête.

practice.prompt: Use the present of habiter for the ongoing state: Elle n'___ plus à Nice depuis deux ans.
practice.explanation: The residence state remains true now.

practice.prompt: Use the negative passé composé of téléphoner with ne ... pas: Nous ___ depuis dimanche. Supply the whole verb group after Nous.
practice.explanation: This states that no call has occurred since Sunday.

practice.prompt: Choose depuis, pendant or en for time needed to finish: Elle a réparé le vélo ___ une heure.
practice.explanation: En expresses the time taken to complete the repair.

practice.prompt: Supply the three-word expression meaning ago: J'ai déménagé ___ cinq mois.
practice.explanation: Il y a locates an event five months before now.

practice.prompt: Supply the contracted preposition/article using à + le: ___ Nouvel An.
Supply à with the required article: ___ Toussaint.
practice.explanation: The phrase is à la Toussaint.

practice.prompt: Supply à with the festival article: ___ Saint-Jean.
practice.explanation: The implied fête is feminine despite Jean being a male saint.

practice.prompt: Supply Saint or Sainte in the festival name: à la ___-Catherine.
practice.explanation: Sainte follows the female saint's name; la refers to the feast.

practice.prompt: Use the present of fumer: Je ne ___ plus depuis mon déménagement.
practice.explanation: An ongoing non-smoking habit is described in the present.

practice.prompt: Use the passé composé of voir: Je ne l'___ pas depuis vendredi.
practice.explanation: No seeing event has occurred since Friday. The unspecified direct-object l' allows masculine vu or feminine vue.

practice.prompt: Use à, adding an article only if required in the usual festival expression: ___ Pâques.
practice.explanation: The usual phrase here is à Pâques, without an article.

practice.prompt: Choose depuis or pendant for a completed period: J'ai vécu à Lyon ___ quatre ans, puis je suis parti.
practice.explanation: The stay is presented as a completed duration.

production_task.prompt: Update a friend about your schedule. Describe one habit that has stopped and remains stopped, one event that has not occurred recently, and two future dates using different holiday expression patterns.
production_task.model_answer: Je ne travaille plus le samedi depuis janvier. Je n'ai pas reçu mon nouvel horaire depuis notre dernière réunion. Nous serons disponibles à Noël. L'association prévoit aussi un repas à la Saint-Patrick.
production_task.translation: I haven't worked on Saturdays since January. I haven't received my new schedule since our last meeting. We will be available at Christmas. The association is also planning a meal on Saint Patrick's Day.
rubric: Use a present form for the continuing changed habit.
Use the compound past for the missing completed event.
Choose each festival's complete preposition/article expression.
Make the dates and timeline understandable.
